name: Converse
seo_title: Converse Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 2 Events, 1 Free
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Converse, TX: Pancakes and Pictures with Santa at Converse Central Fire Station, plus the city's parade and tree lighting.
lede: Converse keeps its Christmas close to home: the city lights its tree at City Hall after an evening parade, and the Converse Fire Department flips pancakes and hosts Santa at its central station on Toepperwein Road.
celebrates: The City of Converse opens its season with the Christmas Parade and Lighting of the Tree at City Hall, 406 South Seguin Road. The city's posts promise a youth choir, food trucks, hot chocolate and activities for kids. A week later, the Converse Fire Department hosts its annual Pancakes and Pictures with Santa at Converse Central Fire Station, with a Letter to Santa station for children. The Parks and Recreation Commission runs a Christmas house decorating contest, and the Converse Police Department collects gifts through its Silver Angel Tree. The library adds a pajama storytime in December.
lastyear: In 2025 the Converse Christmas Parade rolled on Sunday, November 30. The Converse Cougars PTO, which built a float that year, wrote that the parade started at 6:30 pm and ended with the tree lighting at City Hall. The fire department's Pancakes and Pictures with Santa has run for several years, and the Converse Citizen Firefighters say past mornings included musical performances, a craft station, a Letters to Santa area and pictures with Santa, with every breakfast sold helping the department.
facts: Converse is named for Major Converse, chief engineer of the Southern Pacific Railroad, who bought the townsite in 1877, according to the Texas State Historical Association. A post office opened in 1878. German farmers settled the area, and the town's Salatrillo Liederkranz was a German singing society. The Handbook of Texas says Converse was reported to have the oldest 4-H Club in Texas. The 2020 census counted 27,466 people. The city's 2019 newsletter called that year's event the 5th Tree Lighting Celebration.
trains: Converse owes its name to the railroad: the Handbook of Texas says Major Converse, chief engineer of the Southern Pacific Railroad, bought the townsite in 1877. The nearest Amtrak stop is the San Antonio station at 350 Hoefgen Street, served by the Sunset Limited and the Texas Eagle. Train fans can visit the San Antonio Railroad Heritage Museum in Elmendorf on Saturdays, ride the Longhorn and Western Railroad at the Texas Transportation Museum in San Antonio, or take the Hill Country Flyer from Cedar Park.

kidfact: Converse got its name from a railroad man. Major Converse was the chief engineer of the Southern Pacific Railroad, and he bought the land for the town in 1877.
faq: When is the Converse Christmas parade?

The City of Converse holds its Christmas Parade and Lighting of the Tree on a Sunday evening in late November. The parade ends at Converse City Hall at 406 South Seguin Road, where the tree is lit. The city posts the year's date and times on its calendar and Facebook page, so check there before you go.
Where can kids see Santa in Converse?

The Converse Fire Department hosts Pancakes and Pictures with Santa at Converse Central Fire Station, 602 Toepperwein Road, on a Saturday morning in early December. Firefighters serve pancakes, Santa poses for pictures, and children can write to the North Pole at a Letter to Santa station. Pancakes and pictures are priced separately.
Does Converse have a Christmas lights contest?

Yes. The City of Converse Parks and Recreation Commission runs a Christmas House Decorating Contest each year. Converse residents register their homes for free, judges drive by in mid December, and the top three homes win H-E-B gift cards and yard signs. The contest has run for ten years.
How did Converse get its name?

The Texas State Historical Association says Converse is named for Major Converse, chief engineer of the Southern Pacific Railroad, who bought the townsite in 1877. German farmers settled the area, and a post office opened in 1878. Today Converse is a city of more than 27,000 people northeast of San Antonio.
Where is the nearest Amtrak station to Converse?

The nearest Amtrak station is in San Antonio at 350 Hoefgen Street. Amtrak's Sunset Limited and Texas Eagle stop there. For a train ride with kids, the Texas Transportation Museum in San Antonio runs its Longhorn and Western Railroad, with rides included in museum admission.
